### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, activities A21–A25 each appeared in about 85% of traces; in the later window, each appeared in about 18–19% of traces. Conversely, A26–A30 each appeared in about 16% of traces earlier and about 82–83% later. [OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, OCC013, OCC014, OCC015]
- A04 appeared in about 56% of traces earlier and 12% later. A02, A06, A08 and A10 each rose from about 2–4% participation to about 14–19%. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- A20’s outgoing transition was mostly to A24 earlier (84%) and to A29 in 15%; later it was mostly to A29 (82%) and to A24 in 18%. [DIR006]
- A38’s outgoing transition was split between A04 (54%) and A39 (45%) earlier; later it went to A39 in 89% and to A04 in about 1.5%. [DIR011]
- A04’s outgoing transition was almost exclusively to A39 earlier (95%); later it was spread across A19 (25%), A37 (12.5%), A16 (12.5%), A39 (12.5%) and several smaller targets. [DIR002]
- A04 co-occurred with A21–A25 in about 47% of traces earlier but only about 1% later; its co-occurrence with A26–A30 stayed low (about 9% earlier, 11% later). [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011]
- A20 co-occurred with A21–A25 in about 85% of traces earlier and about 18% later; with A26–A30 it co-occurred in about 16% earlier and about 82% later. [REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, REL023, REL024]
- A21 and A26 were mutually exclusive earlier (A21 only 84.5%, A26 only 15.5%, co-occurrence 0%); later A26 only dominated (81.5%) and A21 only dropped to 17.5%. [REL029, REL030]
- A26–A30 co-occurred with A34, A38 and A39 in about 16% of traces earlier and about 82% later. [REL079, REL080, REL081, REL085, REL086, REL087]
- The lag between A38 and A39 was 1 step in 45% and 2 steps in 55% of cases earlier; later it was 1 step in 91% and 2 steps in 9%. [LAG010]
- A04’s mean position moved from near the end of the trace (0.94) to the middle (0.50), but this rests on only 24 traces in the later window. [POS001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a hypothesis that the process shifted from a path that executed activities A21–A25, with A20 leading to A24 and A38 handing over to A04, to a path that executes A26–A30, with A20 leading to A29 and A38 handing over to A39. This is supported by the large, consistent changes in participation, co-occurrence and successor distributions across many activities. A competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out is that the two windows reflect different case types or a change in case mix rather than a modification of a single process.

Other differences: A02, A06, A08 and A10 increased from about 2–4% to 14–19% participation, and A04’s position moved earlier; these may be part of the same shift but are not required for the main hypothesis.
